title: 부부 함께 운동하면 닮아 갈까요? 부모님 두 분 걷기
description: 부부 함께 운동하는 습관은 서로 닮아요. 72쌍을 7일 동안 잰 연구에서 한 사람이 앉아 있는 시간은 배우자와 함께 움직였어요. 부모님 두 분이 같이 걷도록 돕는 법을 정리했어요.
image_alt: 부부 함께 운동하듯 단풍 든 동네 횡단보도 앞에 나란히 서서 걸을 채비를 하는 노부부의 뒷모습을 그린 수채화
image_prompt: Soft watercolor illustration of an elderly Korean couple standing side by side at a crosswalk on an autumn neighborhood street lined with yellow and red trees, seen from behind. No writing, letters or numbers.
body_markdown:
명절에 본가에 갔더니 아버지는 소파에서 텔레비전을 보시고, 어머니도 그 옆에 앉아 계셨어요. 저녁을 먹고 나서도 두 분 모두 한참을 그대로 앉아 계시더라고요. 한 분이라도 먼저 일어나 산책을 나서시면 다른 분도 따라 나서실까, 그런 생각이 들었어요.

한눈에 보는 답부터 말씀드릴게요. 부부 함께 운동하는 습관은 연구에서도 서로 닮는 모습이 나타났어요. 72쌍의 중년과 노년 부부에게 7일 동안 활동 측정기를 채운 연구에서, 한 사람이 오래 앉아 있는 시간은 배우자가 앉아 있는 시간과 뚜렷하게 함께 움직였어요[3]. 또 부부 중 한 사람이 생활 습관을 바꾸면 다른 사람도 같은 변화를 할 가능성이 높아졌다는 연구들이 있어요[1].

## 부부는 정말 생활 습관이 닮아 갈까요?

네, 여러 연구에서 부부의 건강 습관은 서로 닮는 모습을 보였어요. 한 고찰 연구는 부부가 처음부터 비슷한 사람끼리 만나기도 하고, 함께 살면서 점점 닮아 가기도 한다고 설명했어요[1]. 몸무게, 혈압, 흡연, 음주, 그리고 몸을 움직이는 정도까지 약하거나 중간 정도로 서로 관련이 있었다고 해요[1].

우리나라 연구도 있어요. 22개 병원의 가정의학과를 찾은 40세 이상 부부 520쌍, 모두 1,040명을 조사했더니 운동이 부족한 것, 식사가 불규칙한 것, 아침을 거르는 것처럼 건강에 좋지 않은 습관을 부부가 함께 가지고 있는 경우가 많았어요[5]. 남편에게 고혈압이 있을 때 아내도 고혈압이 있을 오즈비는 1.88이었어요[5]. 오즈비는 1보다 클수록 함께 나타나는 경향이 크다는 뜻이에요.

## 한 사람이 많이 앉아 있으면 배우자도 그럴까요?

앉아 있는 시간은 특히 닮는 모습이 뚜렷했어요. 앞서 말씀드린 72쌍 연구에서 한쪽 배우자의 앉아 있는 시간은 다른 배우자의 앉아 있는 시간과 통계적으로 의미 있게 이어져 있었어요[3]. 흥미로운 점은 부부 사이가 얼마나 각별한지와는 상관없이 이런 관련이 나타났다는 거예요[3].

반면 숨이 조금 찰 만큼 걷는 활동이나 걸음 수는 앉아 있는 시간보다 닮는 정도가 약했어요[3]. 그러니까 「같이 운동 나가요」보다 「같이 일어나요」가 먼저 닮아 가는 셈이에요. 텔레비전 앞에서 함께 앉아 계신 시간이 길다면, 그 시간을 함께 줄이는 것부터 시작해 볼 수 있어요.

## 부부의 건강은 숫자로도 함께 움직일까요?

몸의 숫자에서도 부부가 함께 움직이는 모습이 보였어요. 국민건강영양조사 2019~2021년 자료로 부부 1,824쌍을 살핀 우리나라 연구에서, 두 분 모두 대사증후군이 있는 부부는 10.7%였어요[4]. 근력 운동이 부족한 습관을 부부가 함께 가지고 있을수록 두 분 모두 대사증후군이 있을 가능성이 높게 나타났고, 남편의 경우 걷기가 부족한 것도 관련이 있었어요[4].

한 지역 사회 연구에서는 중간 나이가 61세인 부부 231쌍을 살폈어요[6]. 담배를 피우지 않기, 적당한 몸무게, 충분한 신체활동 같은 심장 건강 지표를 배우자가 3가지 이상 지키고 있으면, 본인도 3가지 이상 지킬 오즈비가 3.0이었어요[6].

당뇨도 비슷했어요. 부부 75,498쌍이 담긴 연구들을 모아 분석했더니, 배우자에게 당뇨가 있으면 본인의 당뇨 위험이 26% 높은 것과 관련이 있었어요[2]. 연구진은 부부가 함께 먹는 것과 움직이는 습관을 고쳐 가도록 서로 돕는 것이 도움이 될 수 있다고 덧붙였어요[2].

## 부부가 함께 하면 운동을 더 오래 이어 갈까요?

함께 하면 더 꾸준히 이어 가는 모습이 보였어요. 부부 두 사람 모두를 대상으로 한 프로그램에서는, 배우자가 함께 참여할 때 당뇨 예방 프로그램을 더 잘 지켜 나갔다고 해요[1]. 다만 부부 함께 하는 방식과 혼자 하는 방식을 직접 견준 무작위 비교 연구는 아직 부족하다고 연구진도 밝히고 있어요[1].

이 연구들은 대부분 한 시점을 살핀 관찰 연구라서, 배우자가 원인이라고 단정할 수는 없어요. 그래도 한 분의 작은 변화가 다른 분께 번질 수 있다는 점은 부모님 두 분께 함께 말씀드릴 좋은 이유가 돼요.

## 자주 묻는 질문

**Q. 부모님 중 한 분만 걷기를 좋아하시면 어떻게 할까요?**
연구에서는 한 사람의 행동 변화가 배우자의 같은 변화로 이어질 가능성이 높아졌어요[1]. 걷기를 좋아하시는 분이 먼저 나서실 때 다른 분께 짧게라도 함께 가자고 권해 드리는 것부터 시작해 보세요.

**Q. 두 분이 얼마나 걸으시면 될까요?**
세계보건기구는 65세 이상 어르신께 일주일에 중간 강도 신체활동 150~300분과 일주일에 2일 이상 근력 운동을 권해요[7]. 권고량을 다 채우지 못해도 조금이라도 움직이는 것이 아무것도 하지 않는 것보다 낫다고 해요[7].

**Q. 부부가 함께 운동하면 병이 덜 생기나요?**
부부의 습관과 건강 지표가 함께 움직인다는 관련은 확인됐지만, 함께 운동해서 병이 줄어드는지는 연구로는 아직 알 수 없어요[1].

## 오늘 해 볼 작은 걸음

걷기는 두 분이 세상과 다시 이어지는 문이에요. 부부 함께 운동을 권할 때 자녀가 할 일은 잔소리가 아니라 같이 걷자는 한마디예요.

- 저녁 식사 뒤 텔레비전을 켜기 전에 두 분이 함께 집 앞을 10분 걸어 보시도록 권해 드려요.
- 두 분 중 먼저 걷기를 좋아하시는 분께 「다른 분도 같이 모시고 나가 주세요」라고 부탁드려요.
- 다음 전화 때 「오늘 두 분이 같이 걸으셨어요?」라고 여쭤보며 두 분의 평소를 함께 들어 보세요.

sources.title: Partnership and marriage and risk of type 2 diabetes: a narrative review.
sources.text: In this review, we discuss how partnership and marriage influence cardiometabolic risk factors and risk of type 2 diabetes, and how couple-based approaches to type 2 diabetes prevention might complement individual-focused prevention efforts. There is some evidence that being married per se has a small positive effect on type 2 diabetes risk. Moreover, there is spousal concordance for many type 2 diabetes risk factors due to assortative mating and convergence during partnership, with weak to moderate correlations found for anthropometric measures, blood pressure, lipid concentrations, smoking, alcohol consumption and physical activity level. A meta-analysis shows that people have a higher risk of type 2 diabetes if their spouse has diabetes (OR 1.72, 95% CI 1.47, 2.02). However, despite some evidence, there is still a lack of research on similar associations in relation to progression to type 2 diabetes and diabetes complications. Several studies have suggested that behaviour changes, for example smoking cessation or weight loss, in one partner increase the likelihood that the other partner will make the same changes. Subsequent studies of couple-based interventions that focus on both partners have shown that people are more likely to adhere to a diabetes prevention programme if their partners are also involved in the programme. However, the effect of the quality of marriage on the outcome of an intervention is still unclear. Couple-based interventions are promising, but there is a lack of RCTs comparing couple-based interventions with individual-centred interventions.

sources.title: Spousal diabetes as a diabetes risk factor: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
sources.text: BACKGROUND: Diabetes history in biologically-related individuals increases diabetes risk. We assessed diabetes concordance in spouses (that is, biologically unrelated family members) to gauge the importance of socioenvironmental factors. METHODS: We selected cross-sectional, case-control and cohort studies examining spousal association for diabetes and/or prediabetes (impaired fasting glucose or impaired glucose tolerance), indexed in Medline, Embase or Scopus (1 January 1997 to 28 February 2013). Effect estimates (that is, odds ratios, incidence rate ratios, and so on) with body mass index (BMI) adjustment were pooled separately from those without BMI adjustment (random effects models) to distinguish BMI-dependent and independent concordance. RESULTS: Searches yielded 2,705 articles; six were retained (n = 75,498 couples) for systematic review and five for meta-analysis. Concordance was lowest in a study that relied on women's reports of diabetes in themselves and their spouses (effect estimate 1.1, 95% CI 1.0 to 1.30) and highest in a study with systematic assessment of glucose tolerance (2.11, 95% CI 1.74 to 5.10). The random-effects pooled estimate adjusted for age and other covariates but not BMI was 1.26 (95% CI 1.08 to 1.45). The estimate with BMI adjustment was lower (1.18, 95% CI 0.97 to 1.40). Two studies assessing between-spouse associations of diabetes/prediabetes determined by glucose testing reported high concordance (OR 1.92, 95% CI 1.55 to 2.37 without BMI adjustment; 2.32, 95% CI 1.87 to 3.98 with BMI adjustment). Two studies did not distinguish type 1 and type 2 diabetes. However given that around 95% of adults is type 2, this is unlikely to have influenced the results. CONCLUSIONS: Our pooled estimate suggests that a spousal history of diabetes is associated with a 26% diabetes risk increase. Recognizing shared risk between spouses may improve diabetes detection and motivate couples to increase collaborative efforts to optimize eating and physical activity habits.

sources.title: Spousal Concordance for Objectively Measured Sedentary Behavior and Physical Activity Among Middle-Aged and Older Couples.
sources.journal: Research quarterly for exercise and sport
sources.text: PURPOSE: Although it has been proposed that 1 spouse's health behaviors might correlate with the other spouse's health behavior among married couples, few studies have focused on sedentary behavior. This study examined whether objectively measured sedentary behavior and physical activity are correlated with each other and whether attachment to one's spouse moderates such correlations among middle-aged and older married couples. METHODS: Seventy-two couples participated in the survey. This study measured time engaged in sedentary behavior and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), step counts by an accelerometer for 7 days, and attachment to one's spouse, age, education, and frailty by questionnaires. RESULTS: Multiple regression analyses showed that the sedentary behaviors of 1 spouse statistically significantly regressed on those of the other spouse (β = .30-.47). The regressions of husbands' MVPA and step counts on those of their wives were statistically marginally significant (β = .22-.25), while the regressions of wives' MVPA and step counts on those of their husbands were not statistically significant (β = .15-.18). The interaction terms of the attachment with one's spousal accelerometer variables on those of the other spouse were not statistically significant (β = -.02 to .16). CONCLUSIONS: This study revealed that sedentary behaviors were correlated with each other among couples and attachment to one's spouse did not moderate these correlations. Sedentary behaviors of 1 spouse might influence the other, regardless of attachment to one's spouse. The concordance for physical activity was weaker than that for sedentary behavior.

sources.title: Concordance of Characteristics and Metabolic Syndrome in Couples: Insights from a National Survey.
sources.text: Background and Objective: There is insufficient evidence on whether the concordance of sociodemographic, behavioral, and nutritional characteristics between spouses correlates with the concordance of metabolic syndrome (MetS) between spouses, or if a spouse's characteristics are directly linked to their own MetS. This study seeks to evaluate the association between the concordance of characteristics and the concordance of MetS in couples and investigate whether a spouse's attributes are linked to their partner's MetS. Methods: Analyzing data from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2019-2021, 1824 couples with complete data, including MetS parameters, sociodemographic details, health behaviors, and dietary information, were included. General linear model and logistic regression were employed. Results: Among couples, 10.7% exhibited concordant MetS, with spousal concordance ranging from 1.3% to 81.5% for nonoptimal characteristics. Multivariate analysis revealed that the odds of both partners having MetS increased by 1.04-1.61 times with a higher mean age of the couple and higher concordance in lower education, poor subjective health, insufficient strength exercise, and excessive carbohydrate consumption. When accounting for both individual and spousal factors, the odds of MetS rose with the higher mean age of the couple, having a spouse with MetS, their own characteristics (lower education, poor subjective health, insufficient strength exercise, and sedentary behavior for husbands and wives; alcohol consumption and insufficient walking for husbands; and excessive carbohydrate intake for wives), and spousal factors such as smoking (in husbands) and lower education, lower economic status, and excessive carbohydrate intake (in wives). In wives, spousal sedentary behavior and poor subjective health were linked to decreased odds. Conclusions: The findings suggest a connection between MetS concordance and shared characteristics in couples, as well as an association between both spousal MetS status and characteristics and their own MetS.

sources.title: Spousal Concordance regarding Lifestyle Factors and Chronic Diseases among Couples Visiting Primary Care Providers in Korea.
sources.text: BACKGROUND: Few studies have been conducted in Korea on concordance regarding chronic diseases and lifestyle factors among couples. We, therefore, evaluated spousal concordance regarding lifestyle factors and chronic diseases among Korean couples. METHODS: A total 1,040 participants (520 couples) who visited family physicians were recruited from 22 hospitals. All participants were aged ≥40 years. Participants completed questionnaires on smoking, drinking, physical activity, and irregular eating habits, including skipping breakfast. We estimated the spousal concordance regarding lifestyle factors and chronic diseases using McNemar tests and logistic regression analysis. RESULTS: The concordance rate was high among couples who shared unhealthy behaviors, such as low physical activity, irregular diet, and skipping breakfast (P<0.05). When cardiovascular risk factors such as overweight (odds ratio [OR], 1.73; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.14-2.63), hypertension (OR, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.23-2.86), or hyperlipidemia (OR, 2.41; 95% CI, 1.60-3.64) were prevalent among husbands, the odds that their wives also had the same risk factors at the same time was significantly high. The odds of being depressed when the spouse was depressed were also significantly high in both men (OR, 5.54; 95% CI, 2.19-13.96) and women (OR, 4.52; 95% CI, 1.77-11.53). CONCLUSION: There was a high level of concordance regarding lifestyle factors among couples, which could lead to an increase in the prevalence of chronic diseases among couples. In addition, if a spouse has depression, the odds of their partner also having depression was high.

sources.title: Ideal Cardiovascular Health Metrics in Couples: A Community-Based Study.
sources.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
sources.text: BACKGROUND: Determination of the correlation of ideal cardiovascular health variables among spousal or cohabitating partners may guide the development of couple-based interventions to reduce cardiovascular disease risk. METHOD AND RESULTS: We used data from the HeartSCORE (Heart Strategies Concentrating on Risk Evaluation) study. Ideal cardiovascular health, defined by the American Heart Association, comprises nonsmoking, body mass index <25 kg/m2, physical activity at goal, diet consistent with guidelines, untreated total cholesterol <200 mg/dL, untreated blood pressure <120/80 mm Hg, and untreated fasting glucose <100 mg/dL. McNemar test and logistic regression were used to assess concordance patterns in these variables among partners (ie, concordance in achieving ideal factor status, concordance in not achieving ideal factor status, or discordance-only one partner achieving ideal factor status). Overall, there was a low prevalence of ideal cardiovascular health among the 231 couples studied (median age 61 years, 78% white). The highest concordances in achieving ideal factor status were for nonsmoking (26.1%), ideal fruit and vegetable consumption (23.9%), and ideal fasting blood glucose (35.6%). The strongest odds of intracouple concordance were for smoking (odds ratio, 3.6; 95% confidence interval, 1.9-6.5), fruit and vegetable consumption (odds ratio, 4.8; 95% confidence interval, 2.5-9.3) and blood pressure (odds ratio, 3.0; 95% confidence interval, 1.2-7.9). A participant had 3-fold higher odds of attaining ≥3 ideal cardiovascular health variables if he or she had a partner who attained ≥3 components (odds ratio 3.0; 95% confidence interval, 1.6-5.6). CONCLUSIONS: Intracouple concordance of ideal cardiovascular health variables supports the development and testing of couple-based interventions to promote cardiovascular health. Fruit and vegetable consumption and smoking may be particularly good intervention targets.

sources.title: WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour (2020)
sources.text: 65세 이상 어르신 권고: 일주일에 중간 강도 유산소 신체활동 150~300분 이상, 또는 고강도 75~150분 이상. 중간 강도 이상의 근력 운동을 일주일에 2일 이상. 기능적 균형과 근력을 강조한 복합 신체활동을 일주일에 3일 이상(기능을 높이고 낙상을 막기 위해). 앉아 있는 시간을 줄이고 어떤 강도든 신체활동으로 바꾸는 것이 건강에 이롭다. 권고량을 채우지 못하더라도 조금이라도 하는 것이 아무것도 하지 않는 것보다 낫다.
